newsitem.title: UK: Standard Life cuts bonuses, cites low inflation.
newsitem.headline: Standard Life cuts bonuses, cites low inflation.

text.p: British pensions and insurance group Standard Life Assurance Company said on Thursday it had cut bonuses on its endowment, life and individual pension policies because of lower inflation.
Standard Life said annual growth rates on unitised with profit policies had been reduced.
"This reflects the fact that we expect to continue in a lower inflation environment than the past," Jim Stretton, chief executive of British operations said in a statement.

For its endowment and whole of life policies, the rate on unitised with profit policies was cut to 6.00 percent per annum from 6.5 percent. On individual pension policies, the bonus rates on unitised with profit policies were cut to 7.5 percent per annum from 8.0 percent, Standard Life said.
